findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock, so waiters redo the full load
findings.body: After Lock() at line 48, the function unconditionally reads and parses assets-manifest.json and then overwrites entryPointAssetsCache at line 69. It does this even when a goroutine that held the lock just before has already populated the cache. On a cold start, or after a failed load, N concurrent requests queue on the write lock and each performs the full file read and JSON decode, one after another. The redundant work existed before this change, but the lock now serializes it, so request latency grows with the number of waiters. Re-checking entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock in the non-dev case would complete the double-checked pattern that the RLock fast path starts.

findings.title: Dev mode now serializes every request through the exclusive lock
findings.body: When cfg.Env == setting.Dev, the RLock fast path at lines 45-47 is never taken, so every GetWebAssets call acquires the exclusive write lock at line 48 and holds it across the file open, JSON decode and cache write. Concurrent dev-mode requests that previously ran in parallel are now fully serialized. The impact is limited to local development, but the change in concurrency behaviour is not mentioned and could be avoided by only taking the write lock when a reload is actually needed.

findings.title: No regression test for the concurrent access fix
findings.body: The change fixes a data race on the package-level entryPointAssetsCache, but no test is added. The race is only detectable by calling GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines under `go test -race`. A test that uses a temporary static root with a valid assets-manifest.json, runs concurrent calls in both dev and non-dev configurations, and checks the cache behaviour would prevent a regression. Without it, removing the RWMutex would not be caught by CI.
